items.q: Why are sub-agents a distributed system?
items.a: An orchestrator, concurrent workers, **shared mutable state** and merged results—with only **string in, string out** as the interface.

items.q: What does a half-finished sub-agent look like?
items.a: It **doesn't crash**—it returns fluent text with the **same shape as success**.

items.q: What does a timeout actually tell you?
items.a: Nothing certain: slow, crashed or lost reply look the same, so record it as **unknown**.

items.q: Why don't three agreeing sub-agents prove a claim?
items.a: They read the **same shared guess**—it's **one source counted three times**.
Every fact carries its **source, version and read time**, and decisions use only **fresh** facts.

items.q: How do you make retries safe (A)?
items.a: Give each effect an **identity**, approve it once, and **read back the outcome instead of replaying**.
A **gate and bounded wait** per downstream, where a **refusal counts as a failure**.
Every handoff ends in a **named state**—completed, partial, stale or unknown—not just text.

items.q: How should the orchestrator treat sub-agent output?
items.a: As **untrusted input**: check schema, evidence and freshness, and **recompute the numbers**.

items.q: Why was 'error rate fell from 10/1000 to 6/600' refused?

items.a: When a sub-agent only **drafts text a person reads** before anything happens.
